import.problem.DUPLICATE_ACTIVE_TRIP.fix: The same patient already has this ride on this date, between the same two addresses, in the same window. If this row IS that trip, put its TripId on the row so it updates the existing one instead of duplicating it. If it is a different journey, change the day, the window or one of the addresses. If it is neither, leave it out of the file.
import.problem.TRIP_CANCELLED.title: The trip exists, but it is cancelled
import.problem.TRIP_CANCELLED.fix: A cancelled trip is not brought back by importing it again — that would put a vehicle on a route for a journey the office had closed. Uncancel it from the trips list, or book it as a new trip with a TripId of its own.
The patient cannot be told apart

With no rider ID, the patient is matched on name plus phone. A name on its own would merge two people who happen to share one, and each would see the other's trips. Add the rider ID, or the phone number.
import.problem.INVALID_TRIP_ID.title: The row has no TripId
import.problem.INVALID_TRIP_ID.fix: The TripId is what an import is matched on. Without it, a trip that already exists cannot be told apart from a new booking, so nothing can be stored. Take it from the broker's file.
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RIDER_ID.title: That rider ID belongs to another patient
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RIDER_ID.fix: Somebody else is already filed under this rider ID. It is nearly always a typo in the file. Correcting it here fixes this row; if the file has it wrong on every row, fix it there and import again.
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RECORD.title: Another uniqueness rule refused it
import.problem.DUPLICATE_RECORD.fix: Something in this row already exists and may only exist once, and it is not one of the cases this screen knows how to explain. Export the row and send it to support with the reference below.
import.problem.INVALID_REFERENCE.title: It points at something that is not there
import.problem.INVALID_REFERENCE.fix: The row names a payer, a space type or a patient that does not exist in the system. Check the payer chosen at the top of this screen first — that is the usual cause.
import.problem.MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD.ti: Something it cannot be stored without is empty
import.problem.MISSING_REQUIRED_FIELD.fi: Fill in the fields below. A trip needs at least an identifier, a date, a patient and both addresses.
import.problem.FIELD_TOO_LONG.title: An address is longer than the column
import.problem.FIELD_TOO_LONG.fix: Addresses are stored up to 450 characters. Shorten it: dropping the country, or a floor and suite number that the comment already carries, is usually enough.
import.problem.CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT.titl: Something else was touching the same record
import.problem.CONCURRENCY_CONFLICT.fix: Nothing is wrong with this row. Send it again.
import.problem.TIMEOUT.title: The database did not answer in time
import.problem.TIMEOUT.fix: Nothing is wrong with this row. Send it again — and if it keeps happening, wait a couple of minutes first.
import.problem.INTERNAL_ERROR.title: The server could not say what went wrong
import.problem.INTERNAL_ERROR.fix: This one is ours, not the file's. The reference below is the key to the full record on the server — send it to support. Importing the file again is safe, and is sometimes enough.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_TRIP_ID.title: The row has no TripId
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_TRIP_ID.fix: Caught before anything was sent. The TripId is what an import is matched on — without it a trip that already exists cannot be told from a new booking. Take it from the broker's file.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_PATIENT_IDENTITY: The patient cannot be told apart
Caught before anything was sent. Add the rider ID or the phone number: with neither, two patients who share a name become one record, and each would see the other's trips.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_DATE.title: The row has no usable date
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_DATE.fix: The date column is empty, or it is in a format this layout does not use. Set the day here, or fix the column in the file and import it again.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_ADDRESS.title: One end of the journey is missing
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_ADDRESS.fix: A trip needs both a pickup and a dropoff address. Fill in the one that is empty.
import.problem.LOCAL_ADDRESS_TOO_LONG.ti: An address is longer than the column
import.problem.LOCAL_ADDRESS_TOO_LONG.fi: Caught before anything was sent. Addresses are stored up to 450 characters — dropping the country, or a floor and suite that the comment already carries, is usually enough.
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_COORDINATES.titl: The address could not be located
import.problem.LOCAL_NO_COORDINATES.fix: A warning, not a rejection — the trip was imported. But one end of the journey has no position, so it cannot be routed or shown on a map. Correct the address here, or find it later with the 'missing coordinates' filter on the trips list.

import.problem.LOCAL_MAPPING_FAILED.fix: The format of the file is wrong on this line — a shifted column, a stray quote, a merged cell. It has to be put right in the file itself; there is nothing here to edit.

import.problem.LOCAL_NOT_CONFIRMED.fix: It may or may not have gone in — the import stopped before the server answered. Send it again: trips are matched on the TripId, so if it did go in it is updated, never duplicated.

warn.far_from_stop.What: The driver pressed Arrive or Perform farther from the stop than allowed.
warn.far_from_stop.Why: The time is recorded where the patient was not. They may have pressed before arriving or after leaving, or the address is in the wrong place on the map.

warn.outside_allowed_hours.Title: Shift outside the allowed hours
warn.outside_allowed_hours.What: The driver was on duty in the app outside the hours their route justifies: before the allowed start or after the allowed end. Those minutes are not paid. None of them: there is no margin in pay.
warn.outside_allowed_hours.Why: Pulling out long before the first trip, or pulling in long after getting back, stretches the shift with no work behind it. The warning deducts nothing: the deduction is already made. It is there to talk to the driver if it repeats.

warn.off_route_miles.Title: Off-route miles
warn.off_route_miles.What: The Pull-out reads well above the vehicle’s last reading.
warn.off_route_miles.Why: The vehicle moved between two shifts with no route: personal use, an unrecorded trip or a mistyped reading.
warn.off_route_miles.When: More than {0} mi since the last reading
warn.odometer_vs_gps.Title: Odometer and GPS do not match
warn.odometer_vs_gps.What: The odometer’s miles and the GPS’s differ more than allowed.
warn.odometer_vs_gps.Why: Both measure the same thing. If they disagree, the reading is mistyped or rounded, or the GPS was off part of the day.
warn.pull_in_impossible.Title: Impossible Pull-in reading
warn.pull_in_impossible.What: The miles from Pull-out to Pull-in are many times what the GPS covered.
warn.pull_in_impossible.Why: It is usually an extra digit or a swapped figure. A single reading like this distorts the fleet’s total.
warn.pull_in_impossible.When: More than {0} times the GPS miles
warn.pull_out_impossible.Title: Impossible Pull-out reading
warn.pull_out_impossible.What: The Pull-out is farther from the vehicle’s last sensible reading than it could have driven.
warn.pull_out_impossible.Why: A vehicle does not cover that many miles between shifts. It is nearly always an extra digit, or the route has another vehicle assigned.
warn.pull_out_impossible.When: More than {0} mi per day since the last sensible reading (up to 7 days)
warn.odometer_backwards.Title: The odometer goes backwards
warn.odometer_backwards.What: The reading is below the vehicle’s previous one, or the Pull-in is below its Pull-out.
warn.odometer_backwards.Why: An odometer never goes down: one of the two readings is wrong.
warn.odometer_backwards.When: Any reading below the previous one
warn.zero_miles_with_trips.Title: Zero miles with trips done
warn.zero_miles_with_trips.What: Pull-out and Pull-in read the same, but trips were completed that day.
warn.zero_miles_with_trips.Why: The reading was copied or made up.
warn.zero_miles_with_trips.When: 0 mi and at least one completed trip
warn.wrong_vehicle.Title: Possibly the wrong vehicle
warn.wrong_vehicle.What: Two routes use the same vehicle and their readings cannot come from one odometer.
warn.wrong_vehicle.Why: A route has a vehicle assigned that is not the one being driven. The reading may be right; the assignment is wrong.
warn.wrong_vehicle.When: Two routes, one vehicle and incompatible readings on one day
warn.open_shift.Title: Shift not closed
warn.open_shift.What: There was a Pull-out and no Pull-in.
warn.open_shift.Why: Without a Pull-in nothing is worked out: the day is missing from the report and from the paid hours.
warn.long_shift.Title: Shift too long
warn.long_shift.What: The real shift is longer than the hours set.
warn.long_shift.Why: Usually the driver forgot the Pull-in and pressed it hours later.

warn.incomplete_gps.Why: That leg’s miles with a patient come from its planned distance. It may only be poor coverage.

warn.no_return_leg.Why: That day is paid up to the Pull-in, even if pressed late. It usually happens when a stop was left unperformed.

info.t.days.Title: Shifts
info.t.days.What: How many closed shifts there are in the chosen dates. A shift is one driver, one line and one day, with its Pull-in done.
info.t.days.Formula: 1 for each row of the list
info.t.paid.Title: Paid hours
info.t.paid.What: The sum of the paid shifts. It is what a driver paid by the hour earns. It is not the time they had the app open: it is the part their route justifies.
info.t.miles.Title: Odometer miles
info.t.miles.What: The miles the vehicles drove, with patients and without. They come from the readings the driver types.
info.t.miles.Formula: Sum of (Pull-in − Pull-out) of each shift
info.t.loaded.Title: Miles with a patient
info.t.loaded.What: The miles with a patient on board, counting each patient: a mile with 1 patient is 1, and a mile with 2 patients is 2. With none, 0. It is what a driver paid per mile earns. Below, the occupancy: the share of the odometer with anyone on board.
info.t.loaded.Formula: Sum of (each leg’s miles × patients on board)
info.t.loaded.Pay: Paid: miles with a patient × per-mile rate
info.t.trips.Title: Trips completed
info.t.trips.What: Trips with both the pickup and the dropoff performed.
info.t.pay.Title: Total pay
info.t.pay.What: What the drivers are paid in these dates. Each driver is paid by the hour or per mile, never both, at the rate they had that day. Only an administrator sees it.
info.t.pay.Formula:
Hourly: paid hours × rate
Per mile: miles with a patient × rate
info.t.pay.Pay: It is the total to pay
info.h.shift.Title: Paid shift
info.h.shift.What: What a driver paid by the hour is paid: the whole paid shift. It starts at the later of the real and the allowed start, and ends at the earlier of the real and the allowed end. The six groups below only say where that time went.
info.h.real.Title: Real shift
info.h.real.What: From when the driver started (the Pull-out inspection, or the Pull-out without one) to the Pull-in.
info.h.real.Pay: Not paid: the paid shift is
info.h.unpaid.Title: Not paid
info.h.unpaid.What: The part of the real shift before the allowed start or after the allowed end. All of it is left out, minute by minute.
info.h.loaded.Title: Time with a patient
info.h.loaded.What: How much of the paid shift had at least one patient on board: from the pickup’s Perform to the dropoff’s. If two trips coincide, the minute counts once.
info.h.loaded.Pay: Not paid on its own: it is part of the paid shift
info.h.inspection.Title: Inspection
info.h.inspection.What: The vehicle inspections on leaving and on getting back, when the Provider has them on. Each counts what it lasted, up to the maximum set (10 min from the factory); the rest goes to “Other”.
info.h.inspection.Formula: What each inspection lasted, up to its maximum
info.h.inspection.Pay: Not paid on its own: it is part of the paid shift
info.h.hourwait.Title: Wait for the hour
info.h.hourwait.What: Arrived at a pickup before its window opened: 15 min before the hour on the way out and 5 min before on a return.
info.h.hourwait.Pay: Not paid on its own: it is part of the paid shift
info.h.patientwait.Title: Wait for the patient
info.h.patientwait.What: With the window open: waiting for the patient, boarding or getting off.
info.h.patientwait.Formula: Perform − (opening or arrival, whichever is later)
info.h.patientwait.Pay: Not paid on its own: it is part of the paid shift
info.h.empty.Title: Driving empty
info.h.empty.What: Driving to a stop with nobody on board, leaving the garage and coming back included.
info.h.empty.Pay: Not paid on its own: it is part of the paid shift
info.h.other.Title: Other
info.h.other.What: The rest of the paid shift: free time between trips, lunch or the long part of an inspection.
info.h.other.Formula: Paid shift − the other five groups
info.h.other.Pay: Not paid on its own: it is part of the paid shift
info.h.patienthours.Title: Patient-hours
info.h.patienthours.What: Each patient’s ride, added up: one hour with two patients is two. It is a figure apart, outside the shift’s sum.
info.h.patienthours.Formula: Sum of (dropoff − pickup) of each patient
info.h.trips.Title: Trips
info.h.trips.What: Trips completed in the shift: pickup and dropoff performed.
info.m.general.Title: The shift’s miles
info.m.general.What: The odometer says how many miles the vehicle drove. They split into occupied (with anyone on board) and empty. Apart, miles with a patient count each patient, and are the ones paid per mile.
info.m.general.Formula:
Odometer = occupied + empty
With a patient = miles × patients
info.m.general.Pay: Miles with a patient are paid, to a driver paid per mile
info.m.odometer.Title: Odometer
info.m.odometer.What: The miles the vehicle drove, between the Pull-out and the Pull-in readings. If one is mistyped, an administrator corrects it from its warning.
info.m.loaded.Title: Occupied miles
info.m.loaded.What: The distance the vehicle drove with anyone on board, one or two: each mile of the vehicle, once. It gives the occupancy and the empty miles. They are not the miles that are paid: those are the miles with a patient.
info.m.loaded.Formula: Sum of the legs with 1 or more patients
info.m.empty.Title: Empty miles
info.m.empty.What: The distance the vehicle drove with no patients. The occupied miles are taken off, not the miles with a patient, because the vehicle drives once the mile that carries two.
info.m.gps.Title: GPS miles
info.m.gps.What: The road by the phone’s positions, leaving out jumps above 100 mph. It checks the odometer.
info.m.gps.Formula: Sum of the distances between consecutive positions
info.m.planned.Title: Planned miles
info.m.planned.What: What the legs of the performed route measured. They are used on legs without GPS.
info.m.planned.Formula: Sum of each leg’s planned distance
info.m.passenger.Title: Miles with a patient
info.m.passenger.What: Each mile times the patients on board: a mile with 1 patient is 1, and with 2 patients is 2. With none, 0. Companions do not count.
info.m.passenger.Formula: Sum of (each leg’s miles × patients on board)
info.m.passenger.Pay: Paid: miles with a patient × per-mile rate
info.m.offroute.Title: Off-route miles
info.m.offroute.What: What the odometer rose between the vehicle’s last reading and this Pull-out: it moved with no route. It is not part of the shift’s miles.
info.r.reliability.Title: Reliability
info.r.reliability.What: How many warnings the shift has. It points at what deserves a look and changes no figure. The colour is the gravest warning’s. The values that set them off are edited in “What do the warnings mean?”.

warn.far_from_stop.How: Straight-line distance between the phone and the address when Arrive or Perform is pressed. Each press is one case.
warn.far_from_stop.Pay: Not by itself. A wrong time at the first or last stop can move the paid start or end.
warn.far_from_stop.Do: Open the cases, look at the drawing and ask the driver. If it is always the same address, fix its position on the map.
warn.outside_allowed_hours.How: Allowed start = 1st stop’s promised hour − drive from the garage − preparation − inspection. Allowed end = last stop’s Perform + drive back + inspection. What is outside is not paid.
warn.outside_allowed_hours.Pay: Yes, but already applied: only what is between the paid start and the paid end is paid.
warn.outside_allowed_hours.Do: Open the detail to see that day’s sum. If the driver had a reason to leave early, check the promised hour or the route.
warn.off_route_miles.How: Pull-out − the vehicle’s last sensible reading.
warn.off_route_miles.Do: Check who moved the vehicle. If the Pull-out is mistyped, correct it right here.
warn.odometer_vs_gps.Pay: No: what is paid per mile are the miles with a patient, which do not come from the odometer.
warn.odometer_vs_gps.Do: See whether the reading is rounded or mistyped and correct it. If the GPS is very low, the phone had no signal.
warn.pull_in_impossible.How: Odometer miles ÷ GPS miles (or planned, without GPS). Only if they are also more than 25 mi apart.
warn.pull_in_impossible.Do: Ask the driver for a photo of the dashboard and correct the reading. The suggestion uses the GPS.
warn.pull_out_impossible.How: Pull-out − last sensible reading, against the miles allowed for each day without readings.
warn.pull_out_impossible.Do: Correct the reading. If it repeats, the route may have another vehicle assigned.
warn.odometer_backwards.How: New reading below the last sensible one, or Pull-in below Pull-out.
warn.odometer_backwards.Do: Correct the wrong one. The vehicle’s history shows which does not fit.
warn.zero_miles_with_trips.How: Pull-in = Pull-out and at least one completed trip.
warn.zero_miles_with_trips.Do: Ask for the real reading and correct the Pull-in.
warn.wrong_vehicle.How: Two routes with the same vehicle on the same day, and readings farther apart than the impossible Pull-out limit.
warn.wrong_vehicle.Do: Fix which vehicle each route has in Data → Scheduling → Runs. Do not correct the readings if they are right.
warn.open_shift.How: Pull-out performed, Pull-in not, and the hours since leaving.
warn.open_shift.Pay: Yes: without a Pull-in the shift is not worked out and does not enter pay.
warn.open_shift.Do: Ask the driver to do the Pull-in. It is accepted the next day too.
warn.long_shift.Pay: Not by itself: the paid end is limited all the same.
warn.long_shift.Do: Check whether they forgot the Pull-in. If “Shift end without a limit” also appears, those hours are being paid.
warn.incomplete_gps.How: Some leg with fewer than two GPS positions: its planned distance was used.
warn.incomplete_gps.Pay: Yes, for a driver paid per mile: that leg’s miles with a patient are the planned distance.
warn.incomplete_gps.Do: Nothing to do if it is a one-off. If it is always the same driver, check the phone’s location permission.
warn.no_return_leg.How: No drive back was kept: usually some stop was left without a Perform.
warn.no_return_leg.Pay: Yes: it is paid until the real Pull-in, with no cap.
warn.no_return_leg.Do: Look at the unperformed stops in the detail. If the Pull-in was late, those hours are being paid.
